comment: 2026-10-25 (user): one confidence scale for every decided value, so a reviewer can trust the number the same way everywhere: >= 0.80 good, 0.50-0.80 passable, < 0.50 bad -> flagged for manual review. A confidence is never a fixed constant: it starts from the model's probability for the value it decided (or the rule's own strength where no model exists), backing keywords lift it, and each reason for doubt multiplies it by a penalty below. modules/confidence.py applies this file. 2026-11-14 (user): Final values follow rule_2026_11_14 below instead.

bands.note: good: >= good. passable: >= review. Below review the value is flagged (needs review).

agree_note: Keywords or rules that back the same value lift the model's probability p toward 1: p + (1 - p) x agree_lift x support, support in [0, 1] (a strong title term 1.0, a weak body hint near 0). A model at 0.6 backed by a strong keyword reads 0.8; with no keyword it stays 0.6.
penalties_note: keywords_disagree: the keywords / rules point to a different value than the one decided. no_model: a rule decided with no model to back it (or the model was unavailable). fallback: nothing decided it; a default filled it (Others, General, family default F2F, scan order kept with nothing to confirm it). conflict: other pages / sources of the same document or page say something else. overturned: a later pass reversed the first decision. handwritten: the page is handwritten (OCR is weaker). thin_text: the page has fewer than thin_text_chars characters of text. degraded: an optional dependency was missing and a stand-in decided.
calibration_note: Per module, optional: [[raw, calibrated], ...] knots, piecewise linear, so that a value of 0.8 means right about 8 times in 10 on labelled pages. Empty = identity. Fit from labelled pages, never by hand.
rule_2026_11_14: Section 12 of docs/specials/CONFIDENCE_LOGIC.md (user, 2026-11-14): a Final value's confidence is the deciding model's own probability for the value it chose (no agree_lift, no penalties). backup_low: a backup technique decided (rules only, keywords only, NER, a neighbour's value, a default). flipped_low: a rule or veto went against the model's top answer. carried_factor: a value a page took from its document's anchor page = anchor x carried_factor. measured: a measured fact (no ink, no OCR text). pass1_rule: a blank / junk pass-1 text-pattern rule (DistilBERT does not run in pass 1). agree_lift and penalties stay only for rotation, continuity and sequencing (section 12.3).
floor_note: 2026-11-19 (user): no confidence, any field, is shown below this; a lower value is raised to it.
dropped_value_note: 2026-11-22 (user): a value post-processing dropped (a clinic read as the provider, a DOB far from the manifest's): 0.60, or its own score when lower (was flipped_low, 0.30).

duplicate.note: Section 12.2.1. Yes / Partial: max(floor, 1 - match_slope x (1 - s)), s = match score to the original (0.95 -> 0.50). No, s = best match to any compared page: s < clear_below -> 1.0; clear_below..good_until -> 1.0 - good_slope x (s - clear_below); above -> 0.80 - near_slope x (s - good_until), floor; nothing compared -> 1.0.

modules.note: Module-specific numbers that are not penalties: how strongly a kind of evidence backs a value.

member.note: Unused since 2026-11-14 (section 12): member name, DOB and member ID each take their own KV model_score; rules only / NER -> backup_low.

image_preprocess.note: Tesseract OSD's orientation confidence is open-ended (about 0-20): mapped to 0-1 as 1 - exp(-c / osd_scale), so 1 -> 0.28, 3 -> 0.63, 6 -> 0.86, 10 -> 0.96; then backed by how well the page reads as English at the chosen turn (2026-10-26).

evidence.note: 2026-11-21 (user): a blank / junk rule's confidence from its evidence, not a flat number (modules/blank_junk/evidence.py). rule = 0.5 + rule_span x margin x support; logit(c) = rule_weight x ocr_factor x logit(rule) + model_weight x logit(model p for the verdict); ocr_factor = ocr_min_factor + (1 - ocr_min_factor) x OCR match rate. margin: how far past the rule's own cut (0 on it, 1 far past); support: neighbours compared, same OCR engine, share of lines the neighbours' (Junk) or its own (Main). Used for the short-page rules, contents pages, cards and any rule that goes against the model (was 0.60 / 0.40). Then calibration.blank_junk (fit on labelled pages) and the floor.
